To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the skin, particularly the stratum corneum, poses a formidable physical barrier to the penetration of drugs and (b) there is a considerable interest in the use of the skin as a viable site of drug application for both local and systemic effects.
the stratum corneum is a barrier to drug absorption.
1) the stratum cornea acts as a barrier to drug delivery, 2) the use of penetration enhancers can improve drug delivery, and 3) the mechanism of action of these enhancers can vary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formulation of topical and transdermally delivered products for the treatment of dermatological and ophthalmological conditions.
understanding the mechanisms of skin penetration enhancement, and developing and optimising formulations for the delivery of drugs to skin.
the development of new transdermal and topical drug delivery systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the field of penetration enhancement is in a state of flux.
there is no ideal penetration enhancer.
the field of skin penetration enhancement is a dynamic one and is constantly evolving.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is a large body of evidence that penetration enhancers can improve the delivery of drugs across the skin.

the penetration of drugs across the skin can be enhanced by the use of appropriate vehicles, prodrugs, ion pairs, supersaturation, complexation, partitioning, liposomes, particles, hydration, chemical enhancer, and by the use of a combination of these methods.
transdermal drug delivery is a promising approach to deliver drugs to a variety of tissues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the skin is a very dynamic structure, which can be modified in a controlled manner.
the use of a single penetration enhancement strategy is not sufficient to improve drug permeation through the skin, and that the combination of two or more strategies may be more effective.
the penetration enhancer is not a single molecule but a complex system that is able to interact with the skin in different ways.
